title: Introduce priority-prefetch lanes and adaptive backpressure for async workers
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Context: Our current async workers (Redis consumer groups and Kafka consumers) use a single prefetch window and uniform retry/shaping rules. This causes head-of-line blocking for high-priority small-latency requests and amplifies retry storms during transient downstream errors. Several incidents in Q4 highlighted slow tail latency during bursts and amplified cost due to retries. Goal: Split the worker topology into priority-prefetch lanes (low-latency lane + throughput lane), introduce an adaptive backpressure controller that shapes inflight messages based on measured service time and queue depth, and unify retry semantics with tenant-aware jitter and circuit windows. This ticket implements the runtime and orchestration changes required for Redis and Kafka stacks, upgrades the redis client to the latest stable release that supports async pipelining improvements, and includes performance cleanup on worker hot paths.
acceptance_criteria: Low-latency lane reduces 95th percentile generation tail latency by >= 20% for requests marked priority=latency
System-wide retry storms reduced: number of automatic retries per failing request decreased by >= 60% during transient outages without increasing error surface
CPU and memory overhead of additional prefetch lanes stays under +8% on p4d testbeds
Feature gated with runtime flag and can be toggled per-deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)
Canary rollout completed against 5% of production traffic with no regression in request success rate or cost surge
plan: Phase 1 - design and simulation: build simulation harness to model arrival patterns and backpressure controllers (2 wks)
Phase 2 - runtime changes: implement priority-prefetch queues, add inflight counters and per-lane token buckets (3 wks)
Phase 3 - integrations: wire changes into Redis consumer adapters and Kafka consumer shim, upgrade redis client to 1.12.0, and add config flags (1 wk)
Phase 4 - staging tests: run scale tests on staging fleet, verify metrics, tune thresholds (1 wk)
Phase 5 - canary & rollout: incremental traffic ramp, monitor, rollback plan (2 wks)
Phase 6 - cleanup: deprecate old prefetch config paths and document operational runbook (1 wk)
decisions: Use two-lane topology (latency lane + throughput lane) instead of many priority levels to limit complexity and scheduling overhead
Controller will be centralized per-worker-process (not a global controller) to simplify ownership and improve local reactivity
Retry semantics: implement tenant-aware exponential backoff with capped attempts + randomized jitter; global rate limiter will be applied to retries during detected incident windows
Upgrade redis client to 1.12.0 for async pipelining and connection pooling improvements; this introduces a minor API change in our consumer shim that we will adapt to in the same change
Feature gated behind runtime config and an opt-in config map for Private deployments to avoid surprise behavior for customers
risks: Risk of misconfigured thresholds causing either underutilization (too conservative backpressure) or regression in throughput (too aggressive shaping)
Client upgrade could introduce subtle behavior changes in connection handling under network partitions; we will pin and run stress tests
Increased codepath complexity may temporarily raise bug surface; we will keep the old path behind a flag until post-rollout stabilization
Cross-tenant fairness: priority lanes might be abused if callers mark everything as high priority; we will add enforcement hooks at API gateway and per-tenant quota checks
rollout: Enable feature flag in staging and run the synthetic benchmark suite for 48 hours
Canary 5% prod traffic for 24 hours with automated rollback on latency/cost/error SLO breaches
Progressively increase to 20% then 50% over one week while monitoring throttles, retries, and queue lengths
After 100% enablement, keep the old prefetch window toggled for 2 weeks before full removal
Notify customers of behavior change in dedicated/private deployments and provide config migration guide
monitoring: Dashboards: add per-tenant and per-route SLO dashboards, alert when 95th latency regresses > 10% versus baseline
A/B comparison dashboard for canary vs baseline including cost per 1k tokens
